newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU assembly threatens to block EU-Belarus accord.
newsitem.headline: EU assembly threatens to block EU-Belarus accord.

text.p: The European Parliament warned on Thursday it would block a planned trade and aid pact between the European Union and Belarus unless the Minsk government undertook genuine political and economic reform.
An EU-Belarus agreement "will only be approved when clear steps towards democratic, legal and economic reform are taken by the government in Belarus, the EU assembly said in a resolution.
All international agreements concluded by the EU must have the approval of the 626-member European Parliament and the 15 EU governments before they can take effect.

The parliament complained that Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko had adopted an increasingly "dictatorial style of government" which raised serious questions about future EU relations with the former Soviet republic and with its giant neighbour, Russia.

The EU has already signed a wide-ranging cooperation agreement with Russia but members of the parliament fear the recent strengthening of ties between Minsk and Moscow will adversely affect this relationship.

Belarus and Russia signed on April 2 a charter outlining measures to integrate their two states but the EU assembly says it will not recognise the union treaty as legitimate until Belarus's parliament has been consulted.

Members accused Lukashenko of "completely disregarding the democratically elected parliament, strongly repressing any opposition to his regime and wholly opposing any reform in favour of civil society and economic reform".
If the union treaty did go ahead, the EU's executive European Commission would have examine the consequences for the EU's partnership agreements with Minsk and Moscow, they said.
